name: Ceftazidime-avibactam
executiveSummary: Ceftazidime + β-lactamase inhibitor. Adult **2.5 g IV every 8 h** (2 g + 0.5 g). Pediatrics ≥3 months: **50–62.5 mg/kg every 8 h** of product (max **2.5 g**). MDR/carbapenemase reserve.
indications:
## Indications

- Infections by carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (KPC/OXA-48 and selected AmpC/ESBL) and selected Pseudomonas — per susceptibility.
- cIAI, cUTI, HABP/VAP and other serious infections when alternatives are lacking.

## Precautions

- Restricted / ID use. Renal adjustment; on HD days dose **after** dialysis.
- Infusion **≥2 h**. Prepare and start promptly (≤30 min after reconstitution per label).
- Avoid probenecid; caution with nephrotoxins.

> Dose = total **ceftazidime + avibactam** (4:1).

adulto.dose: **2.5 g IV every 8 h**. Adjust by CrCl per label (reduce dose/interval in renal failure).
adulto.administration: Reconstitute 10 mL SW; dilute in 100 mL NS/D5W; infuse **120 min**.
adulto.notes: ~148 mg Na+/vial. Do not delay infusion start after preparation.

pediatrico.dose: 3–6 months: **50 mg/kg every 8 h** (product). >6 months–18 years: **62.5 mg/kg every 8 h** (max **2.5 g**/dose).
pediatrico.notes: Often not recommended <3 months — check local authorization.

stability:
## Stability

- Reconstituted: dilute and use immediately.
- Diluted: ~24 h refrigerated (label).
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, headache, candidiasis, positive Coombs, eosinophilia, ↑ liver enzymes, phlebitis/fever at infusion site.
